_comment: The committed set of mandatory-question ids. threat-models/README.md and STACK.md §8 H-4.
Data, not Python, so that adding an archetype is a content change (NFR-6) and AC-4's
'no script changes' stays literally true. tests/test_threat_models.py never names a file
here: it globs threat-models/*.md, extracts the ids, and compares against this in both
directions. A file or id missing from here fails; an entry here with nothing behind it
fails too, which is what a rename leaves behind.
Discovery alone would not do: if the expected set were whatever is found, deleting a
question would shrink both sides and stay green — the silent narrowing H-4 exists to
Ids are append-only. A superseded question says so and keeps its id, because the id is
what a later milestone cites: M9's report states which questions were asked, and a
finding cites the question it came from. Removing a line here is the deliberate act.
